title: Day 65 · Week 9, Day 2 — Physiology: the placenta is in her blood — cell-free DNA, the man who found it looking for cells, why the test waits for ten weeks, the fetal fraction her weight dilutes, the ninety-nine point seven that is real, the positive predictive value that depends on her age, the results that found cancer in the mother, and the cup of coffee that now lasts eight hours
summary: Week 9, Day 2 is post-fertilization day 51, Carnegie stage 21 (22–24 mm), the stage at which the cortical plate emerges. Today is the physiology behind cell-free DNA screening (NIPT). Placental DNA circulates in the mother's plasma: found by Lo in 1997 in 80% of women carrying boys; shown by Alberry 2007 to come from the trophoblast, not the fetus (normal levels in anembryonic pregnancies); cleared with a 16-minute half-life (Lo 1999), so the reading is live. Fetal fraction is a median 10% at 10 weeks (Wang 2013, 22,384 pregnancies), which is why the test waits until Day 70; it falls with maternal weight, from 11.7% at 60 kg to 3.9% at 160 kg, with 7.1% of women at 100 kg below the 4% floor (Ashoor 2013), and 56% of failed draws succeed on redraw. Counting performance for trisomy 21: 99.7% detection, 0.04% false positives (Gil 2017); in 15,841 routine pregnancies cfDNA found 38/38 Down syndrome cases vs 30/38 for standard screening, with 0.06% vs 5.4% false positives and a positive predictive value of 80.9% vs 3.4% (Norton 2015, NEXT). PPV depends on maternal age: from Morris 2002 and Snijders 1999 baselines with Gil's rates, roughly 70% at 25, 78% at 30, 90% at 35, 97% at 40 — and far lower for the sex chromosome conditions. False positives come from confined placental mosaicism, maternal copy-number variants, vanished twins and maternal cancer (Hartwig 2017); multiple-aneuploidy patterns flagged cancer in 18% of such results (Bianchi 2015) and 48.6% of women with unusual or non-reportable results had an occult cancer on whole-body MRI (Turriff 2024). A no-call is followed up, not ignored (ACOG PB 226). Sex from Y-chromosome fragments: 95–99% sensitivity depending on gestation (Devaney 2011). Coda: caffeine half-life rises from 3.4 to 8.3 hours in pregnancy (Knutti 1981; Yu 2016).
action: Ten minutes tonight, and nothing to decide. One: on the Questions page of the Day 61 file, add question seventeen in three parts: 'Do you offer cell-free DNA screening, from which week do you draw it, and does the lab report fetal fraction and its no-call policy?' Two: on the same page, write the line that will matter if a result comes back: 'A positive means the chance, at her age, is about ___ percent; a confirmatory test is CVS or amniocentesis; a no-call is followed up, not ignored.' Leave the blank for the OB or fill it from today's numbers. Three: if your partner's weight is over about 100 kg, write 'draw at 11–12 weeks, not 10' beside the question, with Ashoor's 7% as the reason. The deciding — whether to have it, what you'd do with it, who wants to know the sex — is the Day 68 Protocol episode. Tonight is only the understanding.
